answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. When a job completes, the counterparty signs an outcome receipt; repeated receipts from distinct bonded agents raise an identity’s rate limits, while proven fraud burns its bond. Creating sybils then means locking real capital in every shale-thin persona, and coordinating fake receipts requires risking bonds across the network’s karst-like layers. A raven can copy a name, but not cheaply copy trusted history.
